title: Tenant egress isolation leak after peering route reconciliation
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Several Dedicated customers reported intermittent cross-tenant reachability where traffic from Tenant A egressed into Tenant B's VPC after a peering reconciliation event. Impact included occasional request routing to the wrong backend, elevated latencies, and one support escalation from a high-revenue customer that required mitigation within hours. This ticket tracks the investigation, hotfix, and follow-up hardening work to prevent recurrence.
root_cause: During automated VPC peering reconciliation (triggered by route updates from our control plane), host-level egress SNAT rules were momentarily rebuilt in a global chain. Because conntrack entries and per-tenant network namespaces were not reconciled atomically, some packets were matched against the wrong MASQUERADE rule and subsequently forwarded into a peer's route table. Contributing factors: (1) order-of-operations in the reconciliation job caused iptables/nftables chains to be cleared and re-applied without namespace isolation; (2) conntrack table entries persisted across the brief rule replacement window; and (3) asymmetric routing in multi-AZ scenarios exposed stale ARP/neighbor state causing traffic to take an unexpected egress path.
mitigation_applied: 1) Temporarily disabled automatic peering reconciliations for affected tenants to stop ongoing leakage. 2) Deployed emergency patch to add per-tenant ip rule + iptables chain with explicit netns mark so rules are applied atomically. 3) Ran conntrack flush for impacted flows and triggered neighbor garbage-collection on affected hosts. These actions restored isolation within ~30 minutes for impacted tenants.
permanent_fix_plan: - Implement atomic update path: render per-tenant chains in tmp location and swap with atomic iptables-restore/nft - Add conntrack flush hook as part of peering change workflow - Introduce a netns-scoped iptables model (per-host per-tenant) that uses packet marks for unequivocal matching - Add pre/post reconciliation verification step that simulates a small canary and checks for cross-tenant connectivity - Add unit + e2e tests covering peering update sequences in CI
rollout_plan: Canary (5 hosts) -> region (all hosts in single region) -> global. Each stage has rollback steps: revert reconciliation automation, re-enable previous rule set, re-run conntrack/neighbor cleanup. We will run the canary during a low-traffic window and monitor for any tenant isolation alerts for 6 hours before expanding.
verification_steps: 1) After deployment, run synthetic probes from a tenant workload to a blackhole IP to validate egress path. 2) Run cross-tenant handshake tests to ensure no connectivity. 3) Confirm conntrack entries are created using expected per-tenant tuple and are flushed on peering changes. 4) Validate no unexpected ARP/neighbor entries remain in host tables.
